question.question: Does SnapshotStore.List return snapshots in descending applied-index order as the interface states, so that the first entry is the snapshot with the highest Index - or does FileSnapshotStore's Term-before-Index comparison return a lower-index snapshot first when two retained snapshots are inversely ordered, so that the leader ships and a restarting node restores an older applied state than the store actually holds?
question.importance: The first list element is the snapshot the leader opens in sendLatestSnapshot to bring a lagging follower up to date and the first one NewRaft's restoreSnapshot tries to load. Selecting a lower-index snapshot because its last-entry term is higher can ship an outdated snapshot or restore an older applied state, which for a local storage duty is a state-recovery concern rather than a consensus-safety claim; the interface wording fixes the required order regardless of the consequence.
contexts: FileSnapshotStore with retention >= 2 holding two snapshots whose (term, index) positions are inversely ordered
Leader replication goroutine running sendLatestSnapshot for a far-behind follower
Node startup running restoreSnapshot over the same store
event_paths: snapshot store Create(version,index,term,...) -> sink Close -> directory renamed into place with meta.json
r.snapshots.List() -> getSnapshots reads each meta.json, skips .tmp and unreadable entries, sorts with sort.Reverse(snapMetaSlice)
snapMetaSlice.Less compares Term first, then Index, so the reversed order puts the higher-term snapshot first even when its Index is lower
sendLatestSnapshot -> snapshots[0].ID -> r.snapshots.Open(snapID) -> InstallSnapshot to the follower
NewRaft -> restoreSnapshot -> tryRestoreSingleSnapshot for each listed snapshot until one succeeds -> setLastApplied(snapshot.Index)

supporting_behavior_ids.B-snapshot-install: Consumer/consequence: the leader's sendLatestSnapshot opens snapshots[0] to ship to a lagging follower and NewRaft's restoreSnapshot loads the first snapshot that succeeds, so the list order decides which snapshot is sent or restored and therefore which applied state the peer or the restarting node adopts.

counterevidence: Within a single log lineage, terms are non-decreasing with index, so snapshots taken from one node's own log are ordered consistently by both comparators
The SnapshotStore interface is caller-implementable, so only the in-repository FileSnapshotStore is bound by this comparator
List returns at most the retain count and skips unreadable or unsupported snapshots, which limits how many entries can participate
NewRaft's restoreSnapshot falls through to the next listed snapshot when one fails to load, so a bad first choice does not necessarily prevent startup
unknowns: Whether a node can retain two snapshots whose positions are inversely ordered, for example a local snapshot with a high last-entry term next to a snapshot installed from a leader whose last entry has a lower term but a higher index
Whether selecting the lower-index snapshot in restoreSnapshot regresses applied state or makes the startup configuration scan fail on logs that were compacted up to the higher index
Whether the term-first comparator is deliberate authority ordering, in which case only the interface description is wrong
question.trigger_rationale: The interface document and the comparator are two different statements of the same ordering obligation, and they disagree exactly when term order and index order are inverted across two retained snapshots - a situation the code neither prevents nor checks. Because the disagreement depends on a data configuration (which snapshots the store retains) rather than on a single call path, the obligation must be fixed and the comparison tested with snapshots created in the inverted order.
